records.region: Kivalliq, Nunavut; northwestern Ukkusiksalik interior to the Brown River–Brown Lake–western Ford Lake setting.
records.candidate_name_role: bounded lower/middle river component and potential representative system candidate
records.material_pending_reason: The selected northwestern feeder and its entry into the mapped Brown River trunk remain unestablished; the middle/lower corridor, Brown Lake passage and western Ford Lake terminal setting are supported.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The plan separately depicts Brown River in the western park, Piksimanik River farther east and the Sila Lodge corridor. Neither eastern river is substituted for the selected western approach. Brown Lake and Ford Lake are distinct labeled waters. The broad sequence supports a Brown River component candidate, but not the particular upper feeder or all modeled connections.
records.completion_scope: All 31 supplied parts of the single mainstem fragment were considered. The independently issued Parks Canada management plan supports Brown River as a bounded candidate, its eastward and southeastern river corridor, the lower Brown Lake passage and western Ford Lake terminal setting at ordinary corridor scale. Its maps do not establish which actual headward feeder supplies the selected northwestern opening and how that feeder reaches the mapped trunk. That substantive headward gap leaves one source-material-pending record; missing tiny ponds, bends, banks or exact vertices are not separate requirements.
records.supported_name_scope: Parks Canada’s commercial-fishery map names the river corridor west of Ford Lake. Brown River is a potential representative system candidate, with Brown Lake and Ford Lake retaining their distinct component names. The name is not extended to the unestablished selected northwestern feeder.

naming_scope_details.actual_terminal_setting: Western Ford Lake, reached by the lower Brown River corridor; Ford Lake has a separate tidal connection eastward to Wager Bay.

records.region: Northern Yucatán, Mexico; selected inland corridor ending in the Dzilam coastal-lagoon vicinity.
records.material_pending_reason: The inland opening and through-route, transition through coastal wetlands and actual terminal connection remain unestablished. The mapped lagoon–Gulf opening lies southwest of the selected ending.
records.geographic_disambiguation: No representative river-system identity established. Laguna de Dzilam, Bocas de Dzilam and Las Bocas identify a coastal lagoon or its local setting; none is promoted to the name of the selected inland mainstem.
records.completion_scope: All 28 selected parts considered; independent sources establish the regional karst and Dzilam lagoon context, not a continuous selected inland river or the actual final connection.
records.supported_name_scope: No representative river-system identity established. Laguna de Dzilam, Bocas de Dzilam and Las Bocas identify a coastal lagoon or its local setting; none is promoted to the name of the selected inland mainstem.

scope_limits: Regional karst-aquifer connectivity and the general existence of coastal outflows do not establish the selected rendered inland route.
No requirement for hydraulic measurement, current operations, exact bank matching or a single name on every reach was imposed; ordinary mapped through-links would suffice, but were not obtained.

The local study map has limited coastal coverage, and the study-area coordinate in its prose conflicts with its plotted grid. The grid supplies bounded regional orientation, not exact present shoreline placement.
Distinct named reaches could coexist, but no such reach-by-reach identity is established for the selected inland trace.
No source demonstrates that a reservoir, canal, named cenote, managed passage or specific marsh crossing is part of the selected chain. Their presence or absence is not inferred from the model.

records.region: Stonecabin Valley and Mud Lake, Nevada
records.geographic_disambiguation: Representative identity of the selected ephemeral Willow Creek / Stone Cabin Creek drainage through Stonecabin Valley to Mud Lake. DOE explicitly gives both creek names. This does not make Mud Lake or every alluvial distributary thread a creek reach.
records.completion_scope: The one supplied mainstem fragment, all 32 stored parts, chosen northern opening, intermediate tributary joins, upper/lower valley bedrock passage, westward alluvial/playa approach and actual Mud Lake terminal were covered by the independently read 1962 plate and explicit authorial 1962/2008 drainage accounts. The supported representative candidate is Stone Cabin Creek, with Willow Creek as an explicitly source-documented alternative name. No material connector gap or completed name-scope hold remains.

scope_limits: Stone Cabin Creek and Willow Creek equivalence is expressly documented by the 2008 DOE source, but no formal hydronym-registry verification or exact name-boundary adjudication was performed.
The selected terminal is inside a playa. The historical sources establish the natural surface-drainage corridor and conditional runoff connection, not perennial or currently observed through-flow.

Regional/corridor-scale correspondence tolerates the supplied generalized line and individual alluvial-thread differences. It does not certify exact banks, vertices, flow directions on every playa microchannel or modern channel migration.
One USGSTopo original request has an unknown outcome and was excluded entirely; no success, denial or map observation is inferred from it.

records.material_pending_reason: The selected incoming opening, broader river and impoundment through-links, lower junction passages and actual Thames estuary terminal lack ordinary corridor correspondence. Hamilton Reservoir internal passage is supported.
records.geographic_disambiguation: Quinebaug, Shetucket and Thames are distinct source-supported regional reach names. Thames River is a provisional receiving-system lead only; no whole selected-system candidate is established.
records.completion_scope: Bounded current research ended after the usable lake-survey map, three authorial profiles and the recorded guide/plan limitations. Further completion requires affirmatively independent readable corridor cartography; no stopped-source recovery is authorized.
records.supported_name_scope: Quinebaug, Shetucket and Thames are distinct source-supported regional reach names. Thames River is a provisional receiving-system lead only; no whole selected-system candidate is established.

scope_limits: The maps and prose do not assign one natural river name across a reservoir and multiple differently named receiving rivers.
The reservoir map resolves internal lake passage but is not a current flow or dam-operation record.
Absence of operational or exact-bank proof is not itself counted as a material gap. The pending state concerns the genuinely unestablished ordinary selected through-links and terminal coverage.
Uninspected discovery snippets and every unavailable guide/plan body are excluded.
No conclusion is made that these waters lack official or local names.

reconstruction_rule: Start from the pinned r46 cumulative index and apply later append-only deltas in verified commit order, rejecting duplicate IDs. Keep base records, scope clauses, region qualifiers and assessment histories unchanged. Apply explicit status-list changes. Subtract all recorded IDs from the exact eligible initial inventory to recover unrecorded targets; pending IDs remain recorded but are not completed source reviews.
publication_boundary: Own factual name/scope findings, public official URLs, bounded geometry metadata and public continuity pins only. No original maps, crops, complete coordinates or private source/derivative/registration fingerprints. Official hosting does not establish source redistribution rights.

research_order.progress_rule: Follow the actual continental order: Americas, Asia, Africa, Europe, then other, with all rivers before lakes. Preserve original queue IDs and ranks for continuity; apply documented geographic deferrals without counting them as name research, and place deferred objects into their corrected later phase by length-descending, stable-ID order. Prior candidate and scope-held assessments remain unresolved where stated.
